answer: Give every agent a juniper-like reputation root: a single identity that slowly grows one pearl of verified work per epoch, with each pearl's pigment — the visible shade of its grading history — publicly recorded. A newcomer starts pale and untrusted; only sustained, well-graded work deepens the pigment. An attacker spawning a thousand fakes must fund a thousand deposits, wait the same epochs, and produce distinct quality work for each, so forging a credible history costs linearly more per fake while an honest agent pays it once.
